children.text: By immediately showing her acne without makeup or trying to hide her skin, Alix establishes herself as someone willing to be vulnerable with her audience. This is important because beauty influencers are often associated with perfect images, makeup, and carefully edited photos. Instead of beginning the TikTok by presenting an idealized version of herself, Alix shows viewers a more imperfect and realistic version. The fact that she is recording the video while sitting in her bed also contributes to this sense of authenticity. The casual bedroom setting feels personal and less staged than a professional studio, making her appear more relatable and trustworthy. These aesthetics reinforce her ethos because viewers can see her in a more natural environment while also seeing her acne for themselves. The visual and setting together suggest that social media does not always show what someone's skin actually looks like.
As Alix explains what has been happening with her skin, she uses her own personal
experience to create an emotional connection with her audience. Rather than simply giving
skincare advice, she talks about something that has affected her personally, which allows viewers
who experience acne to identify with her. This creates pathos because acne can be connected to
feelings of insecurity, embarrassment, and frustration, especially when appearance is an important
part of someone's social life. By discussing her own experience, Alix shows that even though she
is a successful beauty and lifestyle influencer, she experiences many of the same insecurities as
her audience. This helps break down the distance between influencer and viewer.
